$comment: Enforced budgets for what every session's FIRST request carries, in characters, per persona and harness. Policy, rationale and how to raise a budget live in docs/prompt-budgets.md. This file is the source of truth for the numbers: app/server/src/promptBudgets.ts never hard-codes one. A budget is a tripwire, not a target — raising one with a recorded reason is a normal move.

limits.label: system prompt
limits.covers: every counted prompt layer: the harness base we keep, the persona file with its conditional sections, registry/KB/memory guidance, the profile suffix, project context and assembly framing.

limits.label: eager tool block
limits.covers: name + description + JSON schema of every tool loaded up front, plus the harness builtins we construct. Deferred tools are reported but not counted.

limits.label: first request
limits.covers: the two above — what this persona costs before the user's first word.

raises.why: the delivery loop gains its merge/close step: the persona must state that only a repository-supported method may be chosen, that non-default merge and close-with-reason are pre-authorized, and that a default-branch merge always pauses for human approval
carries the prompt raise above
the same finish-pull-request rules on the pi harness, whose persona layer already sat at 98% of its budget
carries the prompt raise above

the coordinator persona was written as telegraphese to fit 1500 and had grown to 96% of it. v1.4 makes this role the run's standing judgement — asked after every assessment, routing fixers, reviewers and the verdict — so its rules are restated as prose that gives each one its reason, which is what an agent needs to apply a rule to a case the text did not anticipate. It also now says what the role cannot see and that being asked implies nothing about how the work fared.

the same persona file, shared by both harnesses: telegraphese replaced by rules that carry their reasons, plus what the coordinator cannot see and the v1.4 fact that it is asked after every assessment rather than only a passing one.

follows the prompt raise at the same eager tool block; the standing rules and the run-status schema must both be present before the user's first word, and this keeps firstRequest the usual 500 below prompt + eagerTools.
follows the prompt raise at the same eager tool block, keeping firstRequest 500 below prompt + eagerTools so the persona may spend one limit's headroom but not both.

the persona gains the peer-session loop: which runtimes an agent may start helpers on, that a spawned peer is an ordinary session with no watchdog or automatic report, and that the coordinator owns closure — chase a quiet child, route findings back, re-review until the exact target passes, never poll
carries the prompt raise above

the shared chat-images layer: a session artifact may be SHOWN in the reply as a Markdown image rather than named as a path, which needs the URL form, where it comes from, and that no other image source renders

the persona now tells the agent to stop background work it no longer needs; work left running is the signal that it is parked on it, so the rule and its reason both have to be in the prompt

the monitor tool now teaches the filter convention it has no parameter for: stdout is the event stream, never pipe raw logs, cover the failure signatures too. Without it an agent points monitor at a dev server and pays one turn per batch — 31 turns in the session that prompted this — and background bash says plainly that it notifies once, at exit
